title: Rescope Console dashboard + tracing MVP; prioritized feature prune and acceptance criteria
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Summary: Tighten the scope for the initial Console MVP to ensure on-time, reliable shipping while preserving the most critical developer and SRE workflows. This ticket captures the PRD-level scope changes, rationale for each cut, acceptance criteria, and implementation notes for the dashboard, tracing, and route-level cost breakdown features.

Background: The original scope included a broad set of dashboard tiles, full trace sampling for all routes, and per-route token-level cost breakdown for historical queries. Implementation complexity and observational costs have pushed schedule risk. We must reduce surface area so the Core console can ship a focused MVP that supports debugging high severity issues and answering cost questions without unbounded telemetry costs.

Goals:
- Deliver a compact set of high-value dashboard tiles and a single trace viewer that surfaces actionable root causes.
- Provide a lightweight cost breakdown (hourly rollup + top-5 routes) instead of per-request token traces for launch.
- Offer graceful degradation: when trace sampling budget is exceeded, show sampled summary plus an explanation and link to on-demand deep trace workflow.

Scope changes (what we are cutting or delaying):
1) Cut: Full per-token historical cost replay (defer to 'Tracing+Cost v2'). Rationale: high storage/ingest cost and low immediate usage signal.
2) Cut: Cross-route aggregated flame graphs in initial release. Keep single-route flame graphs only.
3) Delay: Custom dashboard builder (defer to post-MVP). Ship fixed tile set configurable by toggles.
4) Cut: High-cardinality tag exploration UI (defer; provide CSV export for now).

What remains in MVP (trimmed surface):
- Fixed dashboard: 6 tiles (P95 latency by route, errors by route, throughput by route, inference cost hour rollup, top-5 most expensive routes, system GPU utilization).
- Trace viewer: single-route trace view with spans, error highlights, KV cache miss markers, and sampling metadata.
- Cost panel: hourly rollup + top-5 route cost table with percent change vs prior period; link to export and archived raw traces for gated investigation.
- Rollout controls: feature toggle to enable/disable tracing at org level; sampling rate selector with sensible defaults; automated graceful degrade when budget thresholds crossed.

Trade-offs and mitigations:
- Trade-off: Reduced fidelity for historical cost debugging. Mitigation: Provide quick export to more detailed logs and a supported on-demand deep trace mode that can be enabled for specific investigations.
- Trade-off: Fewer customization options for dashboards. Mitigation: Provide guardrails (preset tile sets) + roadmap item for a lightweight templating API in v1.1.

Acceptance criteria: See acceptance_criteria field for checklist (must be green before 'In Review').

Artifacts and links:
- PRD (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CONSOLE/pages/PRD-compact-dashboard-mvp
- Design mocks (Figma): https://www.figma.com/file/console-mvp-compact-dash
- Example queries & sample datasets: gs://redwood-console/samples/mvp-launch
- GitHub epic: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/epics/MVP-compact-dashboard
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard: six fixed tiles rendered on orgs with at least one active route; tiles load within 2s on the majority of test traces.
Trace Viewer: single-route trace view shows spans, error highlights, and KV cache miss markers for sampled traces; sampling metadata is displayed and includes budget/trace id.
Cost Panel: hourly cost rollup displays for the last 7 days and includes top-5 route cost table with delta vs prior period and CSV export link.
Graceful Degrade: when org's trace budget falls below threshold, tracing UI shows sampled summaries with a clear explanation and an ‘Request Deep Trace’ CTA that opens an internal ticketing flow.
Rollout Controls: org-level toggle and sampling rate selector are in Console Settings; toggles respect RBAC and persist across sessions.
Performance: median dashboard tile query latency under typical load is <800ms, P95 <2s for the test org dataset used by Eng QA.
Privacy & Security: no raw PII is surfaced in dashboard tiles or trace summaries; security checklist items from security review are signed off (if required).
Telemetry cost: projected telemetry ingest for MVP is within the committed budget (Finance/Infra signoff present).
